successCriteria.description: A new migration adds a nullable `password_hash` column to the `employees` table (up) and drops it (down), following the async up/down convention of `migrations/20260913000000_initial_schema.js`.

`Employee` gains `passwordHash: string | null`, and `PgEmployeeRepository` persists and reads it end-to-end: `EmployeeRow`/`mapRow` carry `password_hash`, every SELECT list and the INSERT column/value + RETURNING lists include it, and `create` persists `input.passwordHash`.
`IEmployeeRepository.findByManagerId(managerId, client?)` returns all employees whose `manager_id` equals the argument (empty array when none), accepting an optional trailing `PoolClient`.

`IEmployeeService` exposes `getEmployeeByEmail`, `getEmployeesByManagerId`, and `getEmployeeProfileById`; `getEmployeeByEmail` throws `NotFoundError` on an unknown email and `getEmployeesByManagerId` delegates to `findByManagerId`.
`getEmployeeProfileById` returns an `EmployeeProfile` (imported from `src/shared/types`) whose mapping never exposes `passwordHash` or `terminationDate`.
Unit tests cover `findByManagerId`, `getEmployeeByEmail` (including the `NotFoundError` case), and assert the profile mapping never leaks `passwordHash`.

constraints: The `password_hash` column must be added as a nullable text column (`t.text`), not `json`/`jsonb`, and the migration must use async `exports.up`/`exports.down` with `knex.schema.alterTable('employees', ...)`.
`Employee.passwordHash` must be typed `string | null` (nullable — an employee may have no login credential yet).
`EmployeeProfile` must be imported from `src/shared/types` — it must not be re-declared or re-exported from the employee module.
The profile mapping must omit both `passwordHash` and `terminationDate`; `passwordHash` must never appear in any returned profile.
`findByManagerId` must filter with `WHERE manager_id = $1` and return an array (possibly empty), never throw when no rows match.
outOfScope: No routes/controllers/RBAC for the employee module in this phase — the `GET /employees/me` route and its wiring belong to Phase 7.
No auth/login logic (bcrypt compare, token minting) — that is Phase 4; this phase only adds the credential column and read surface it depends on.
No audit-log writes (GP-002) — this phase is read-only plus a schema/column addition; no state-changing business operation is introduced.
No refactor of `leave.service.ts`/`balance.service.ts` to import the shared date helpers — that is a later phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: An Employee may exist without a login credential: `passwordHash` is nullable and `null` means no credential is set; it is never synthesized or defaulted to a non-null value by the repository or service.

An EmployeeProfile is a credential-free projection of an Employee: it carries identity/role/employment fields but never `passwordHash` or `terminationDate`, so it is safe to return to any authenticated caller.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching Employee; throws NotFoundError when no employee has that email (delegating to the existing findByEmail).
Returns the (possibly empty) list of direct reports; never throws for an unknown manager id.
Returns an EmployeeProfile for the employee; throws NotFoundError on an unknown id; the returned value never contains passwordHash or terminationDate.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `EmployeeProfile` shape (fields and the absence of `passwordHash`/`terminationDate`) must match the canonical definition in `src/shared/types/index.ts`; the mapping must not introduce a divergent local type.

The migration must follow the async `exports.up`/`exports.down` convention and column style of the initial schema (string/text columns, snake_case), so `password_hash` is consistent with the existing `employees` table.

`EmployeeRow`/`mapRow` and the SELECT/INSERT lists must stay consistent with the existing snake_case↔camelCase mapping in `PgEmployeeRepository`, so `password_hash` is mapped to `passwordHash` exactly like the other columns.
`getEmployeeByEmail` must reuse the existing `IEmployeeRepository.findByEmail` and the existing null→NotFoundError pattern already used by `getEmployeeById`.

`CreateEmployeeInput` (Omit<Employee,'id'>) must now require `passwordHash`; the existing test helper `makeInput` and `FakeEmployeeRepository.create` must be updated to supply/handle it so the suite still type-checks.

integrationPoints.why: The profile mapping's return type is the canonical EmployeeProfile from Phase 1; the employee module must import it rather than re-declare it.
getEmployeeByEmail and getEmployeeProfileById surface unknown-email/unknown-id as the shared NotFoundError, matching existing service error semantics.
findByManagerId must accept an optional trailing PoolClient and fall back to the shared pool, per the transaction-boundary convention.
